title: Invoke endpoints trace_ids input contract: reject empty lists and non-string items with 400, and de-duplicate ids before lookup
answers: Why does issue detection with no traces return a 400 instead of starting a job?
Why does submitting a non-string trace id to the scorer invoke endpoint return a 400 and not a 500?
How are duplicate trace ids handled when running GenAI evaluation or issue detection?
Where is trace_ids validated for the issues/invoke endpoint?
body:
Path: mlflow/server/handlers.py:_invoke_issue_detection_handler, _invoke_genai_evaluate_handler and _invoke_scorer_handler parse the trace_ids list of the invoke requests (issue detection, GenAI evaluation, scorer invocation) before any store lookup or job submission.
Rule: All three /invoke handlers share one trace_ids contract: the schema uses _assert_item_type_string so non-string items fail as validation errors; an empty list raises INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE ('Please select at least one trace...'); and ids are de-duplicated with list(dict.fromkeys(...)) to keep order before the batch lookup. When adding a similar endpoint, copy all three steps so the endpoints stay consistent.
Symptom: issues/invoke with an empty trace_ids list submitted a no-op run and job; scorer/invoke returned a 500 for a non-string trace id (for example a dict or nested list) instead of a 400.
Constraints: Validation runs before the store is consulted, so these 400s do not hit batch_get_trace_infos. The empty-list check is in the handler body, not the schema, because _assert_required permits []. Applies to request validation only; it does not replace the experiment-binding check in _validate_trace_ids_in_experiment.
applies: Request validation for trace_ids on invoke-style handlers in mlflow/server/handlers.py.
says: Issue detection with no traces returns a 400 error instead of starting a job
Scorer invoke returns a server error instead of a bad request when a trace ID is not a string
Duplicate trace IDs in GenAI evaluation or issue detection requests are handled inconsistently
Empty trace list in issue detection submits a pointless run and job
Trace ID input should be validated and de-duplicated the same way across evaluation, issue detection and scorer endpoints
search: Request validation of trace_ids on the issues, GenAI evaluate and scorer invoke endpoints: non-string items fail as validation errors, an empty list returns a 400 INVALID_PARAMETER_VALUE in the handler body, and ids are de-duplicated in order before lookup. Validation runs before any store lookup or job submission. New similar endpoints should copy all three steps.
